documents.unit: University of Montana Teaching and Learning
documents.title: Teaching in the Age of Generative AI
tiers: Collaborative exploration with GenAI tools encouraged
Use of GenAI tools encouraged with attribution
GenAI tools allowed for specific tasks
Limited use of GenAI tools with permission
documents.summary: Teaching-center guidance asking every instructor to put a GenAI statement in the syllabus, with model statements from encouraged to discouraged, instructor-use disclosures, and talking points. It advises against AI detectors and sets out an educative procedure for suspected misuse.
documents.stance_why: The page makes no university-wide rule and instead tells every instructor to "include a brief statement" and supplies five model statements, from "Collaborative Exploration With GenAI Tools Encouraged" to "Use of GenAI Tools Discouraged"; it also gives instructor-use templates, a no-detector rule and a procedure for suspected misuse. The tiers make this delegates.

units.why: The page says how the guidance came about, "developed in response to those requests" from instructors; a statement about how the guidance was made is P84, general phase, informs.
units.anchor: developed in response to those requests

units.why: Names the body that wrote the guidance ("faculty, staff, and administrators") and its scope across programs, so it describes how the policy was made (P84).
units.anchor: faculty, staff, and administrators have created concise, straightforward guidelines

units.why: Discloses that GenAI helped write the guidance itself, which is part of how the document was made (P84); no better type exists for this disclosure.
units.anchor: GenAI was used to summarize and refine language
units.fit_note: Also a disclosure of AI use in producing the guidance, not only a description of the drafting process.

units.why: The guidance is declared provisional ("will continue to change"), which is P54, a revisit-regularly statement.
units.anchor: will continue to change as the needs of our campus change

units.why: Points readers to a library guide on AI, citing and copyright, i.e. library support alongside the page (P72), a recommendation.
units.anchor: explore the Mansfield Library’s
units.fit_note: Points to a library guide (a resource) rather than to a person or service.

units.why: "All instructors should include a brief statement" is a recommendation that every syllabus carry an AI statement, which is P09; modality should because of the word 'should'.
units.anchor: All instructors should include a brief statement in their course syllabus

units.why: The university leaves the stance open ("welcome, limit, or discourage") and sets none itself; this is P04, instructors set the rule.
units.anchor: Whether you welcome, limit, or discourage their use

units.why: Gives a reason for the syllabus statement: it "promotes academic integrity" by marking boundaries. Fits P95 (honesty as the reason) better than P09, which is the duty to include a statement.
units.anchor: boundaries between acceptable assistance and academic dishonesty
units.fit_note: The reason is clarity about boundaries, not fairness to other students.

units.why: The page lists reducing student anxiety as a reason for the statement and says guidance "builds trust"; a reason for communicating expectations (P09), informs.
units.anchor: provides clarity and builds trust
units.fit_note: States a benefit (less anxiety, more trust) of having a statement, not the duty itself.

units.why: Says a transparent statement supports equity because students differ in familiarity with AI; equity of access is P51, though it is not about cost.
units.anchor: supports more equitable GenAI access
units.fit_note: Equity through familiarity and transparency, not through free access or alternatives.

units.why: Says a policy can open discussion of how students can "engage with it meaningfully"; recommends talking about AI with students (P66).
units.anchor: can open the door to discussing not just

units.why: A benefit claim ("support learning, creativity, and critical reflection") with no rule: P87.
units.anchor: GenAI can support learning, creativity, and critical reflection

units.why: Frames the syllabus statement as aligned with institutional goals ("academic excellence and innovation"); an institution-wide framing statement, P56.
units.anchor: we aim to foster both academic excellence and innovation

units.why: The instructor is the one who crafts the policy, P04 (instructors set the rule), informs.
units.anchor: Creating a policy requires deep consideration by the instructor

units.why: Explains that AI is "built in to systems students already use" such as Adobe and Copilot and so hard to track; this is a limit on control (P82). P07 (embedded AI rules) would be a rule; this is only a warning.
units.anchor: very difficult to track and identify
units.fit_note: Also names embedded AI in Adobe PDF reader, library databases and Copilot (P07 content), but states no rule about it.

units.why: Template for courses where GenAI is a learning objective: "encouraged to use" for many tasks, so default is encouraging AI (P02), unit_stance encourage.
units.anchor: encouraged to use generative AI tools to draft, brainstorm, research, revise, and reflect

units.why: Same template makes use conditional on transparency; disclosure of AI use (P24).
units.anchor: but always with transparency
units.fit_note: Template wording says 'transparency' without saying how.

units.why: The template promises class discussion and teaching of ethical use for academic and professional contexts: P44 (teach effective AI use as professional skill).
units.anchor: We will discuss how to use these tools critically and ethically
units.fit_note: Emphasizes critical and ethical use as well as professional use.

units.why: Template: tools "welcome" as aids to learning with responsible use; a default of permitting or encouraging AI (P02).
units.anchor: are welcome in this course as aids to your learning

units.why: Students must acknowledge or cite "substantial AI contributions" such as text, code or analysis, which is P24 with a threshold of 'substantial'.
units.anchor: asked to acknowledge or cite any substantial AI contributions
units.fit_note: Applies only to substantial contributions, not all AI use.

units.why: Template that permits AI only for listed tasks ("summarizing texts, finding sources, generating initial coding ideas"). The narrow list is a restrict stance; listing example tasks fits P15 (exploring approaches) best.
units.anchor: You may use generative AI tools for specific tasks in this course
units.fit_note: Task list also includes summarizing texts and finding sources, and is a narrow permission, not just brainstorming.

units.why: Requires documenting "what tools you used and how"; this names the tool and how it was used, closer to P25 than P24.
units.anchor: you must clearly document what tools you used and how
units.fit_note: Asks for tools and manner of use, not the exact prompt or output.

units.why: Student must verify AI output, "responsible for verifying the accuracy"; P31.
units.anchor: responsible for verifying the accuracy of any AI-generated content

units.why: Template where AI is permitted "only with prior instructor approval": banned unless permitted case by case. That is a restrict stance set per instructor decision, P04 (the permission sits with the instructor) rather than P01.
units.anchor: is permitted only with prior instructor approval
units.fit_note: Approval is requested per use, but the default is no AI.

units.why: Student must consult the instructor before using AI; asking first is P10.
units.anchor: please consult with me first

units.why: Unauthorized use is classed as an academic-honesty violation: P36.
units.anchor: Unauthorized use may be considered a violation of academic honesty

units.why: Template says AI is "discouraged" for all work, but the next sentence treats use as a violation. This sentence alone is P03, discourage without forbidding.
units.anchor: is discouraged for any assignment or activity in this course
units.fit_note: The following sentence in the same template makes use a violation, so it is more than discouragement.

units.why: Students must submit their own original work, P29.
units.anchor: All submitted work must be your own original effort

units.why: Template says use "will be treated as a violation"; P36, with a bans-AI effect (prohibit).
units.anchor: will be treated as a violation of academic integrity policies

units.why: Recommends instructors state their own AI use to students, with the reason: transparency and modeling. This is P47, informs.
units.anchor: Using instructor statements creates transparency

units.why: Template for an instructor who discloses no AI use in the course: P47.
units.anchor: I have not used generative AI tools in the preparation, design, or delivery

units.why: Template commits that AI will not assess student work, apart from Canvas-embedded tools. A human-grades commitment (P46) and also a limit disclosed to students (P47); I choose P46 because of "assess any of your work".
units.anchor: will not use AI tools to assess any of your work
units.fit_note: Also an instructor disclosure to students and carves out Canvas-embedded tools.

units.why: Template statement that no course materials were AI-generated, an instructor disclosure about materials: P48 covers materials; P47 is disclosure of the instructor's own use. Chose P47 because this states no use.
units.anchor: None of the content, resources, or assignment guidelines in this course were generated using AI

units.why: Template that discloses AI help in assignment design: P47.
units.anchor: used AI tools to help brainstorm or refine assignment prompts

units.why: Template for disclosing AI-made materials, P48.
units.anchor: have been created or enhanced using generative AI tools

units.why: The template says AI-made content is reviewed and edited by the instructor, the review half of P48.
units.anchor: All AI-generated content has been reviewed and edited

units.why: Template disclosing AI drafting of announcements; instructor use for teaching work, disclosed: P47.
units.anchor: I occasionally use AI tools to draft routine communications

units.why: Instructor reviews AI-drafted messages before sending; human review of AI output, P59.
units.anchor: always reviewed before being sent
units.fit_note: A review commitment about AI-drafted communications.

units.why: Template disclosing AI-made feedback examples: P47.
units.anchor: feedback or model responses provided in this course may have been generated

units.why: Template commitment to tell students whenever the instructor uses AI: P47.
units.anchor: I will let you know

units.why: Invites students to ask about AI in the class; this is an open channel for questions, P10.
units.anchor: encouraged to ask questions about how AI fits into our classroom practice
units.fit_note: Invites questions about the instructor's AI use generally, not only about whether a use is allowed.

units.why: Offers talking points so instructors introduce the policy in class; P66 (explain and discuss the rules).
units.anchor: a short comment when introducing your syllabus or gen AI policy

units.why: Scripted line telling students that each class has its own policy: P11 (each course's policy governs only that course).
units.anchor: you might have a different gen AI policy in each of your classes

units.why: Script warns that AI output may be "misleading, biased, or inaccurate"; the verification warning is P31.
units.anchor: it can also be misleading, biased, or inaccurate

units.why: Script raises ethical and environmental concerns: P53.
units.anchor: about the environmental impacts of Gen AI

units.why: Script tells students the syllabus carries the AI rules; students check the syllabus. P78 fits (students follow each course's rules) but modality is informs; chosen over P09, which binds instructors.
units.anchor: a short statement in the syllabus about how I expect you to use
units.fit_note: Stated as what the instructor will do, not as a student duty.

units.why: Direct instruction to ask the instructor when unsure: P10.
units.anchor: If you’re ever not sure what’s allowed, just ask me

units.why: "faculty should not use AI detection tools" is a direct rule against detectors; the reason is the lack of an enterprise contract. P39 (do not rely on detectors).
units.anchor: faculty should not use AI detection tools

units.why: Bans uploading student work to unvetted third-party tools on privacy and IP grounds. Student-data protection and vetted tools: P50; P49 is about students uploading, so does not fit.
units.anchor: uploading assignments to third-party tools constitutes an unfair and unapproved use

units.why: Detector output may not be sole evidence; this is an evidence standard (P69). P39 also fits but the specific content is the evidence standard.
units.anchor: should not be used as sole evidence of misconduct

units.why: Explains detectors are unreliable and biased against multilingual and neurodivergent writers, supporting not relying on them: P39, informs.
units.anchor: AI detectors frequently produce

units.why: "Not admissible proof" sets an evidence standard for misuse findings: P69, chosen over P39 as it says what counts as proof.
units.anchor: Detection results are not admissible proof

units.why: Says conversations and context outweigh scores; talk with the student: P57.
units.anchor: Conversations and context matter more than software scores

units.why: Recommends educational, fair responses focused on intent and clarity: P68.
units.anchor: Fair and educational responses

units.why: "a moment for learning, not just discipline" is the educative-response principle, P68.
units.anchor: Treating AI misuse as a moment for learning, not just discipline

units.why: Directs instructors to colleagues and a named staff role for support when handling suspected misuse: P63 (faculty support), also naming an owner.
units.anchor: seek conversation and support from the
units.fit_note: Support is for handling suspected misuse, not for learning AI.

units.why: Before acting on suspected misuse, instructor checks own syllabus clarity. No type covers this pre-action self-check.
units.anchor: Review your syllabus policy to confirm how clearly it was stated
units.uncovered_note: Before acting on suspected misuse, the instructor checks how clear their own syllabus AI policy was.

units.why: An evidence standard: suspicion is not proof, P69.
units.anchor: Suspicion alone is not proof

units.why: Instruction to meet the student privately before escalating: P57.
units.anchor: Schedule a private, non-confrontational meeting with the student

units.why: In the meeting the instructor invites the student to explain their process, which also lets the student respond: P64 (right to respond) fits less well than P57, which is the talk-first step.
units.anchor: Invite the student to describe their process in detail
units.fit_note: Also gives the student a chance to respond.

units.why: First-time or unclear-policy cases are teachable moments: P68.
units.anchor: Treat this as a teachable moment

units.why: Offers revision or resubmission rather than penalty for unintentional use: P68.
units.anchor: offer to let the student revise or resubmit the work

units.why: Instructor documents the interaction ("for your own records") as a procedure step in handling suspected misuse: P81.
units.anchor: protects both you and the student
units.fit_note: Internal record-keeping, not filing a report with a central office.

units.why: The scenario table names a concrete response: no penalty for unintentional use under an unclear policy. Stated penalties in advance: P37.
units.anchor: Education + no penalty or resubmission option

units.why: Names a warning plus resubmission or partial credit, a concrete consequence: P37.
units.anchor: Warning + resubmission or partial credit

units.why: Intentional misuse goes to the formal conduct process: P81.
units.anchor: Proceed with the academic integrity process described in

units.why: Instructors should know the Student Conduct Code reporting procedures: P81.
units.anchor: familiarize yourself with the procedures described in

units.why: Follow-up message that learning, not punishment, is the goal: P68.
units.anchor: learning—not punishment—is the primary goal

units.why: After a case the instructor reinforces trust, which is the presume-good-faith element of P68.
units.anchor: Reinforce your trust in them going forward

units.why: After a case, change syllabus or assignments to reduce ambiguity; redesign of assignments around AI: P35.
units.anchor: modifying your syllabus and/or future assignments to reduce ambiguity

units.why: Suggests process reflections as assignment design: P26 (reflections) is about students submitting them; here the instructor adds them to assignments, so P35.
units.anchor: Add process reflections

units.why: Suggests requiring drafts or outlines to make process visible; assignment redesign, P35.
units.anchor: Require drafts or outlines

units.why: Suggests adding questions on tool use and attribution to assignments; P35.
units.anchor: Include questions about tool use and attribution

units.why: Raises bias as a topic for reflection and student assignments: P53.
units.anchor: reinforce or amplify social biases

units.why: Raises environmental cost as a question for reflection: P53.
units.anchor: environmental costs of developing and running large-scale AI models

units.why: Suggests the ethics questions as assignment topics for students: P35 (assignment design).
units.anchor: potential angles for assignments for students
units.fit_note: Suggests topics about AI itself rather than assignments that restructure work around AI.

documents.title: AI Resources for Faculty
documents.summary: Provost page for faculty on generative AI. It encourages faculty to engage with AI, says what a syllabus statement should cover, and cites the Student Code of Conduct plagiarism definition that now includes AI-derived content. It states UM has no plagiarism detection software and that sanctions are for clear violations.
documents.stance_why: The provost page says approaches "can range from restricting AI use to integrating it" and leaves the choice to instructors, while encouraging faculty to engage with AI and adding the Code of Conduct plagiarism definition. It sets no uniform student stance, so delegates.

units.why: Says resources will be updated regularly while the university studies the effect on learning: P54, with a P55 flavor; chose P54 because no data is cited.
units.anchor: will be updated regularly as we work to better understand the impact
units.fit_note: Also says the university is trying to understand AI's effect on student learning.

units.why: Faculty are "encouraged to engage" with AI, encouraging instructor use: P59.
units.anchor: Faculty are encouraged to engage with these tools
units.fit_note: Encourages engagement in general, not a specific teaching task.

units.why: Ties faculty AI use to existing University Policy 370: P77.
units.anchor: principles outlined in University Policy 370

units.why: Faculty should keep course materials current, including appropriate AI use: P102 (stay informed).
units.anchor: Regularly update your course materials to reflect new developments
units.fit_note: Is about updating course materials as AI changes, not only staying informed.

units.why: Faculty should incorporate AI into teaching to help learning and careers: P44 (AI as professional skill).
units.anchor: incorporate AI ways that enhance student learning and career preparation
units.fit_note: Directs faculty to change their teaching, not students to learn AI.

units.why: Suggests faculty use AI for efficiency on simple tasks: P59.
units.anchor: use AI as an efficiency tool

units.why: Requires equitable access when AI is integrated into courses: P51.
units.anchor: done equitably, ensuring access for all students

units.why: Tells instructors to set clear expectations in syllabi: P09.
units.anchor: set clear expectations for the use of generative AI in your courses

units.why: Instructors choose anywhere from restricting to integrating: P04.
units.anchor: can range from restricting AI use to integrating it as a tool for learning

units.why: States bans cannot be enforced easily: P82.
units.anchor: Banning the use of generative AI is difficult to enforce

units.why: A good syllabus statement should define the scope of acceptable tools: P61.
units.anchor: A clear definition and scope of acceptable tools and their use

units.why: A syllabus statement should tie AI use to learning outcomes: P83.
units.anchor: how they relate to the courses learning outcomes

units.why: The syllabus statement should cover integrity and attribution: P24 as the nearest.
units.anchor: Academic integrity and attribution requirements
units.fit_note: An item on a checklist for what the syllabus statement covers.

units.why: The syllabus statement should cover privacy and data security: P50.
units.anchor: Privacy, Data Security, and Responsible Use
units.fit_note: Checklist item, no content on how to protect data.

units.why: Instructors must set citation standards using MLA, Chicago or APA: P24.
units.anchor: set standards for proper attribution and citation
units.fit_note: Addressed to instructors, who set the attribution standard.

units.why: The Code of Conduct classes AI misrepresentation as plagiarism: P36.
units.anchor: includes Generative AI in the definition of plagiarism

units.why: Quoted code definition forbids presenting AI-derived content as one's own: P19.
units.anchor: content derived directly from a generative artificial intelligence tool

units.why: Fact that no plagiarism detection software is licensed: P39 nearest since no tool is used.
units.anchor: UM does not subscribe to any plagiarism detection software
units.fit_note: States absence of software, rather than unreliability.

units.why: Says there are "few reliable tools" that can prove AI plagiarism, a reason not to rely on detectors: P39, informs.
units.anchor: few reliable tools to detect generative AI

units.why: Notes detector bias against international students: P39 (as part of the reason not to rely on detectors); P53 covers bias but of AI, not detectors.
units.anchor: bias towards the writing of international students

units.why: Says students must be taught AI's utility and limits, which is teaching AI use: P44.
units.anchor: learn the utility and limitations of Generative AI through preemptive instruction
units.fit_note: Includes limitations, and prescribes instruction and corrective assessment.

units.why: Career reason for teaching AI: P44.
units.anchor: vital preparation for their future careers where AI will likely be ubiquitous

units.why: Sets a threshold: investigations and sanctions only for clear violations, an evidence standard (P69).
units.anchor: should be reserved for clear violations
units.fit_note: A threshold on when to investigate, not about the kind of evidence.

units.why: Recommends teaching students that human capacity exceeds AI as the main approach: P32 nearest (students stay the thinker).
units.anchor: human capacity for thought, imagination, and feeling far exceeds
units.fit_note: A message for instructors to teach, not a rule for students.

units.why: Discloses that ChatGPT 4 helped adapt the page, a process statement: P84.
units.anchor: ChatGPT 4 was used to adapt the content on this website
units.fit_note: Also discloses AI use in producing the page.

notes: Coder B. Only the two included university-layer documents were coded. The detector section of montana-1 carries an update note (February 2026).
